newsitem.title: USA: Members of alleged N.Y. drug gang indicted.
newsitem.headline: Members of alleged N.Y. drug gang indicted.

text.p: Thirty-five alleged members of a New York City drug gang were indicted on Thursday, accused of conspiracy, murder and using children as young as 14 years old in their illegal drug operations, prosecutors said.

The gang, known as "112th No Fear" because it operated on 112th Street in Manhattan's Harlem neighbourhood, used children to transport crack cocaine, guns and cash and to act as lookouts, said Manhattan District Attorney Robert Morgenthau.
Recently the gang's crack cocaine and heroin business grossed about $500,000 annually, down from as much as $3 million in previous years, he said.
The 10 accused gang leaders face the possibility of life in prison if convicted. The others face up to 25 years in prison.

According to the indictment, the gang used violence to terrorise drug rivals and fatally shot a drunken neighbourhood man for making too much noise on a street corner where gang members were openly selling drugs.
The gang's arrest "creates a vacuum that people can't go to those locations and buy drugs," said Patrick Harnett, chief of the New York City Police Department's narcotics division.
